summary: Navigate the editor, open a program, run it and enter answers without leaving the terminal.
syntax: F1 Help | F2 Save | F3 Open | F4 Save as | F5 Run | F6 Stop | F7 Input | F10 Quit
parameters: Function keys: use Fn if your keyboard reserves them.
Ctrl+S Save; Ctrl+O Open; Ctrl+N New; Ctrl+Q Quit; Ctrl+C Stop.
Tab/Shift+Tab: move focus; Tab in the editor inserts indentation.
use_cases: Find an example with F3 and run it with F5.
Answer INPUT prompts in the bottom command field.
notes: Escape or F1 closes this help. In the topic list use arrows; in the page use PageDown/PageUp.
Open lists examples; choose a file, Enter to select, Enter again to open. Unsaved edits show *.
Startup animation lasts 5 seconds; a key/click or --no-splash skips it.
Syntax notation: [...] is optional, {...|...} means choose an alternative, and ... means repeat. Do not type notation brackets/braces unless a code example shows them literally.

summary: Display text and numbers; control whether the next item stays on the same line.
parameters: Semicolon (;): no extra separator and suppresses the final newline when last.
Comma (,): advance to the next 14-character print zone.
use_cases: Display answers in calculators.
Build a row of stars inside a loop.
notes: Positive numbers include a leading and trailing space. Formatting is approximate.
PRINT USING, TAB, SPC and PRINT# are not implemented. Colon-separated IF branches keep their own PRINT statements.

summary: Read one line of user input into one or more numeric or string variables.
parameters: prompt: optional quoted text followed by a semicolon; ? is appended.
variable: a scalar or array element; use a $ suffix for strings.
Multiple targets require comma-separated fields in one answer.
use_cases: Ask for principal, rate and time.
Collect a name and an age.
notes: Malformed input raises Redo from start and ends the run; automatic retry is not implemented.
Numeric fields must be plain numbers, without percent/currency symbols. In the UI use the bottom INPUT field.

summary: Assign an evaluated expression to a variable or array element. LET itself is optional.
parameters: variable: name, optionally ending in %, !, # or $.
expression: must have a compatible numeric/string type.
use_cases: Store an interest calculation.
Update a loop accumulator.
notes: % is signed 16-bit, ! and unsuffixed variables are single precision, # is double, $ is a string.
Assignment coerces explicitly; mixing string and numeric types raises Type mismatch.

summary: Choose a branch based on a numeric condition.
parameters: condition: zero is false, any nonzero number is true.
then/else body: statements or a target line; ELSE is optional.
use_cases: Validate input before computing.
Choose pass/fail or profit/loss output.

examples.source:
10 SCORE=75
20 IF SCORE>=60 THEN PRINT "Pass" ELSE PRINT "Try again"

notes: Only single-line IF is implemented; multiline IF/ELSEIF/END IF is not.
Colons after THEN belong to that branch; nested ELSE binds to the closest unfinished IF.

summary: Introduce the branch executed when IF is true.
parameters: body after THEN: statements separated by colons, or a line number.
use_cases: Validate input before computing.
Choose pass/fail or profit/loss output.

examples.source:
10 SCORE=75
20 IF SCORE>=60 THEN PRINT "Pass" ELSE PRINT "Try again"

notes: Only single-line IF is implemented; multiline IF/ELSEIF/END IF is not.
Colons after THEN belong to that branch; nested ELSE binds to the closest unfinished IF.

summary: Introduce the alternative branch of an inline IF.
parameters: body: statements or a target line, executed only when the IF condition is false.
use_cases: Validate input before computing.
Choose pass/fail or profit/loss output.

examples.source:
10 SCORE=75
20 IF SCORE>=60 THEN PRINT "Pass" ELSE PRINT "Try again"

notes: Only single-line IF is implemented; multiline IF/ELSEIF/END IF is not.
Colons after THEN belong to that branch; nested ELSE binds to the closest unfinished IF.

summary: Repeat statements while a numeric counter moves from a start value to an end value.
syntax:
FOR counter = start TO end [STEP step]
    statements
NEXT [counter [, counter ...]]
parameters: counter: numeric scalar, not a string or array element.
start/end: inclusive bounds, evaluated when FOR is entered.
use_cases: Draw triangles with nested row/column loops.
Add or multiply a known number of values.
notes: A positive-step loop with start>end is skipped; a negative-step loop with start<end is skipped.
NEXT must exist. Execution is bounded by --max-steps; zero STEP raises Illegal function call.

summary: Separate the starting and ending values of a FOR loop.
syntax:
FOR counter = start TO end [STEP step]
    statements
NEXT [counter [, counter ...]]
parameters: end: inclusive limit. Direction is determined by STEP.
use_cases: Draw triangles with nested row/column loops.
Add or multiply a known number of values.
notes: A positive-step loop with start>end is skipped; a negative-step loop with start<end is skipped.
NEXT must exist. Execution is bounded by --max-steps; zero STEP raises Illegal function call.

summary: Set the increment or decrement of a FOR loop.
syntax:
FOR counter = start TO end [STEP step]
    statements
NEXT [counter [, counter ...]]
parameters: step: numeric value; use -1 to count down. Zero is rejected.
use_cases: Draw triangles with nested row/column loops.
Add or multiply a known number of values.
notes: A positive-step loop with start>end is skipped; a negative-step loop with start<end is skipped.
NEXT must exist. Execution is bounded by --max-steps; zero STEP raises Illegal function call.

summary: Increment a FOR counter and either repeat its body or finish the loop.
syntax:
FOR counter = start TO end [STEP step]
    statements
NEXT [counter [, counter ...]]
parameters: counter: optional, but when present must match the current innermost FOR.
Multiple names: NEXT J,I closes nested loops in that order.
use_cases: Draw triangles with nested row/column loops.
Add or multiply a known number of values.

examples.source:
10 FOR I=1 TO 2
20 FOR J=1 TO 2
30 PRINT I*J;
40 NEXT J,I

notes: A positive-step loop with start>end is skipped; a negative-step loop with start<end is skipped.
NEXT must exist. Execution is bounded by --max-steps; zero STEP raises Illegal function call.

summary: Repeat a block while its condition is nonzero; test before each iteration.
parameters: condition: numeric expression checked before the body.
use_cases: Repeat until a counter reaches a limit.
Use loops with an unknown iteration count.

examples.source:
10 N=0
20 WHILE N<3
30 N=N+1
40 PRINT N;
50 WEND

notes: A false initial condition skips the body. Infinite loops hit the instruction budget or can be stopped with F6.

summary: Close a WHILE block and return to its condition.
parameters: No arguments. A matching WHILE is required.
use_cases: Repeat until a counter reaches a limit.
Use loops with an unknown iteration count.

examples.source:
10 N=0
20 WHILE N<3
30 N=N+1
40 PRINT N;
50 WEND

notes: A false initial condition skips the body. Infinite loops hit the instruction budget or can be stopped with F6.

summary: Jump directly to an existing numbered program line.
parameters: line: numeric expression yielding an integer line number that exists.
use_cases: Repeat a simple menu.
Skip to a selected section of a numbered program.
notes: Undefined lines raise Undefined line number. GOTO does not save a return location.

summary: Call a numbered subroutine and remember where to return.
use_cases: Reuse the row drawing routine in the diamond example.
Share a calculation without duplicating statements.
notes: Use END before the subroutine area to avoid falling into it. RETURN without GOSUB raises an error.
RETURN line and QBasic SUB/FUNCTION procedures are not implemented.

summary: Resume after the most recent GOSUB.
use_cases: Reuse the row drawing routine in the diamond example.
Share a calculation without duplicating statements.
notes: Use END before the subroutine area to avoid falling into it. RETURN without GOSUB raises an error.
RETURN line and QBasic SUB/FUNCTION procedures are not implemented.

summary: Allocate zero-based arrays with inclusive upper bounds.
parameters: name: array variable, optionally with a type suffix.
upper: nonnegative upper index, not the element count. DIM A(4) has five cells.
use_cases: Store marks for several students.
Store rows and columns of a small grid.
notes: Indices are zero-based. Implicit arrays default to upper bound 10 in each dimension.
Cumulative array capacity is 100,000 cells. Duplicate DIM, bad rank and out-of-range subscripts raise errors.
OPTION BASE, REDIM, AS declarations and user-defined array types are not implemented.

summary: Store literal values in the program for READ statements.
parameters: items: numeric literals (optionally signed) or quoted strings separated by commas.
use_cases: Load a fixed list of scores.
Replay a small table without keyboard input.

examples.source:
10 DATA 5,6,"Ada"
20 READ A,B,N$
30 PRINT A+B;N$
40 RESTORE
50 READ X
60 PRINT X

notes: Unquoted DATA strings and calculated DATA expressions are not supported. READ past the end raises Out of DATA.
DATA is collected before execution, even if the DATA line is skipped by control flow.

summary: Assign the next DATA values to variables in sequence.
parameters: targets: scalar variables or array elements whose types match the DATA values.
use_cases: Load a fixed list of scores.
Replay a small table without keyboard input.

examples.source:
10 DATA 5,6,"Ada"
20 READ A,B,N$
30 PRINT A+B;N$
40 RESTORE
50 READ X
60 PRINT X

notes: Unquoted DATA strings and calculated DATA expressions are not supported. READ past the end raises Out of DATA.
DATA is collected before execution, even if the DATA line is skipped by control flow.

summary: Reset the DATA cursor to the start or to DATA at/after a specified line.
parameters: line: optional existing program line. Without it, restart at the first DATA value.
use_cases: Load a fixed list of scores.
Replay a small table without keyboard input.

examples.source:
10 DATA 5,6,"Ada"
20 READ A,B,N$
30 PRINT A+B;N$
40 RESTORE
50 READ X
60 PRINT X

notes: Unquoted DATA strings and calculated DATA expressions are not supported. READ past the end raises Out of DATA.
DATA is collected before execution, even if the DATA line is skipped by control flow.

summary: Stop execution normally.
use_cases: Finish the main program before subroutine lines.
Stop after validation or a final result.
notes: STOP and END both halt in Ghost BASIC. CONT and resumable STOP are not implemented.

summary: Halt execution at this point.
use_cases: Finish the main program before subroutine lines.
Stop after validation or a final result.
notes: STOP and END both halt in Ghost BASIC. CONT and resumable STOP are not implemented.

summary: Treat the rest of the physical line as a comment.
parameters: comment text: explanatory text that is not executed.
use_cases: Explain a formula.
Leave a practice challenge next to a loop.

examples.source:
10 REM Display a greeting
20 PRINT "Hello" : REM a colon inside this comment is ignored

notes: Comments end at the physical newline. REM text is not parsed as statements. Apostrophe is an alias.

summary: Emit a terminal clear-screen sequence.
use_cases: Clear a compatible batch/prompt terminal between displays.
notes: ANSI clear sequence is emitted; this is not an emulated BASIC screen buffer.
The ASCII IDE filters control escapes rather than clearing its interface.

summary: Emit the ASCII bell character.
use_cases: Request a terminal notification where bells are enabled.
notes: Sound depends on the terminal settings. The IDE filters the bell; synthesized audio is not implemented.

summary: Execute the current stored program from its beginning.
parameters: No arguments; RUN filename is not supported.
use_cases: Run a program after LOAD or editing.
notes: RUN clears variables, arrays and DATA state. F5 runs the editor buffer in the UI.

summary: Display stored numbered source in sorted order.
parameters: No arguments; line ranges are not supported.
use_cases: Inspect a loaded program.
notes: The UI lists the current editor text. LIST does not execute source.

summary: Load a text source file into the current program.
parameters: filename: quoted path inside the workspace (--root).
use_cases: Load a sample for execution.

examples.output: The file is loaded and listed.

notes: UTF-8/BOM and DOS CP437 text supported; SAVE writes UTF-8. Tokenized/protected files are not supported.
Prompt LOAD requires numbered source. The UI can open unnumbered QBasic text for editing, but cannot execute it.
A failed LOAD keeps the existing source. Files are limited to 1 MB.

summary: Save the current source as UTF-8 text.
parameters: filename: quoted path inside the workspace.
use_cases: Keep changes to an exercise.

examples.output: A UTF-8 source file is written.

notes: Prompt SAVE can overwrite a file. The UI asks before Save as replaces a different existing file.
No tokenized or protected SAVE format; opening a DOS file does not rewrite it.

summary: Start a new source program; the classic prompt also clears variables and arrays immediately.
use_cases: Start a new exercise.
notes: Prompt NEW discards source immediately. The UI asks before discarding unsaved editor changes.
In the UI, NEW replaces the editor buffer; the next RUN resets runtime variables.

summary: Clear variables and arrays without deleting stored source.
parameters: No arguments; classic memory-size arguments are not implemented.
use_cases: Reset immediate-mode calculations.
notes: Supported as a prompt command, not as a numbered-program statement or the UI bottom-field command. Use RUN to reset before execution.

summary: Show the keyword index or a detailed topic.
parameters: keyword: optional statement, function, operator or alias.
use_cases: Learn a keyword without internet access.

examples.output: Syntax, parameters, use cases, examples and notes for PRINT.

notes: F1 opens searchable help in the UI. Planned topics are marked Not implemented.

summary: Exit the programming environment.
use_cases: Leave the prompt or close the IDE.
notes: The UI checks unsaved work. The prompt exits immediately. QUIT and EXIT are aliases.

summary: Exit the programming environment; alias of SYSTEM.
use_cases: Close the environment from its command field.
notes: This is an environment command, not a numbered BASIC statement.

summary: Exit the programming environment; alias of SYSTEM.
parameters: No arguments in the environment command.
use_cases: Leave the classic prompt.
notes: QBasic EXIT FOR, EXIT DO, EXIT SUB and EXIT FUNCTION are separate planned features and are not implemented.

summary: Add two numbers, or concatenate two strings.
parameters: Operands: two numbers or two strings.
use_cases: Build arithmetic formulas or conditions.
Trace how operands change the result.
notes: Both operands must be numeric or both strings; implicit numeric-to-string conversion is not performed.

summary: Subtract numbers; prefix minus negates a value.
use_cases: Build arithmetic formulas or conditions.
Trace how operands change the result.
notes: Exponentiation binds more tightly than unary minus; use (-2)^2 for positive four.

summary: Multiply numeric values.
use_cases: Build arithmetic formulas or conditions.
Trace how operands change the result.
notes: Multiplication precedes addition. Strings cannot be multiplied.

summary: Divide numeric values, preserving a fractional result.
use_cases: Build arithmetic formulas or conditions.
Trace how operands change the result.
notes: A zero divisor raises Division by zero.

summary: Divide rounded 16-bit integer operands and truncate the quotient toward zero.
use_cases: Build arithmetic formulas or conditions.
Trace how operands change the result.
notes: Operands are rounded nearest-even to signed 16-bit before division; out-of-range operands overflow.

summary: Raise a numeric base to a power.
use_cases: Build arithmetic formulas or conditions.
Trace how operands change the result.
notes: Powers associate left in this implementation: 2^3^2 is (2^3)^2. Negative-base fractional powers raise an error.

summary: Return the remainder after integer division.
use_cases: Build arithmetic formulas or conditions.
Trace how operands change the result.
notes: Operands use signed 16-bit nearest-even rounding; remainder follows the dividend sign, unlike Python modulo.

summary: Bitwise complement a rounded signed 16-bit value.
use_cases: Build arithmetic formulas or conditions.
Trace how operands change the result.
notes: NOT binds below comparisons; NOT 1=1 means NOT (1=1).

summary: Bitwise AND of two rounded signed 16-bit values.
use_cases: Build arithmetic formulas or conditions.
Trace how operands change the result.
notes: Both sides are evaluated; AND does not short-circuit. Parenthesize complex conditions.

summary: Bitwise OR of two rounded signed 16-bit values.
use_cases: Build arithmetic formulas or conditions.
Trace how operands change the result.
notes: Both sides are evaluated; OR does not short-circuit.

summary: Bitwise exclusive OR: keep bits set on exactly one side.
use_cases: Build arithmetic formulas or conditions.
Trace how operands change the result.
notes: This is bitwise XOR, not exponentiation; use ^ for powers.

summary: Bitwise equivalence: complement of XOR.
use_cases: Build arithmetic formulas or conditions.
Trace how operands change the result.
notes: True comparisons use -1 (all bits set); both operands are evaluated.

summary: Bitwise implication: NOT left OR right.
use_cases: Build arithmetic formulas or conditions.
Trace how operands change the result.
notes: Signed 16-bit operations; use parentheses when combining comparisons.

summary: Test whether the left value is equal to the right value.
parameters: left/right: both numeric or both strings.
use_cases: Validate entered values.
Choose an IF branch.
notes: Strings compare lexically using Unicode codepoints, not legacy codepage bytes.
= also introduces assignment in LET; within an expression it compares values.

summary: Test whether the left value is not equal to the right value.
parameters: left/right: both numeric or both strings.
use_cases: Validate entered values.
Choose an IF branch.
notes: Strings compare lexically using Unicode codepoints, not legacy codepage bytes.
= also introduces assignment in LET; within an expression it compares values.

summary: Test whether the left value is less than the right value.
parameters: left/right: both numeric or both strings.
use_cases: Validate entered values.
Choose an IF branch.
notes: Strings compare lexically using Unicode codepoints, not legacy codepage bytes.
= also introduces assignment in LET; within an expression it compares values.

summary: Test whether the left value is greater than the right value.
parameters: left/right: both numeric or both strings.
use_cases: Validate entered values.
Choose an IF branch.
notes: Strings compare lexically using Unicode codepoints, not legacy codepage bytes.
= also introduces assignment in LET; within an expression it compares values.

summary: Test whether the left value is less than or equal to the right value.
parameters: left/right: both numeric or both strings.
use_cases: Validate entered values.
Choose an IF branch.
notes: Strings compare lexically using Unicode codepoints, not legacy codepage bytes.
= also introduces assignment in LET; within an expression it compares values.

summary: Test whether the left value is greater than or equal to the right value.
parameters: left/right: both numeric or both strings.
use_cases: Validate entered values.
Choose an IF branch.
notes: Strings compare lexically using Unicode codepoints, not legacy codepage bytes.
= also introduces assignment in LET; within an expression it compares values.

summary: Keep PRINT items on the same line without inserting a print zone.
parameters: No value parameter: this is punctuation between PRINT items.
use_cases: Write a compact line of code.
Understand PRINT formatting and statement boundaries.
notes: A final semicolon suppresses the newline. INPUT also uses a semicolon after an optional prompt.

summary: Separate arguments, array indices or data fields; in PRINT advance to a print zone.
syntax:
PRINT expression, expression
DIM name(upper, upper)
parameters: Meaning depends on context: PRINT, INPUT, function arguments, DIM or DATA.
use_cases: Write a compact line of code.
Understand PRINT formatting and statement boundaries.
notes: PRINT zones are 14 columns in this implementation; there is no automatic screen wrap.

summary: Separate multiple BASIC statements on one numbered line.
parameters: Each separated item is a complete statement.
use_cases: Write a compact line of code.
Understand PRINT formatting and statement boundaries.
notes: After IF THEN, colon-separated statements stay in that branch; comments consume the rest of the physical line.

summary: Return the nonnegative magnitude of a number.
use_cases: Find an absolute difference.
notes: ABS removes a negative sign; it does not round.

summary: Return -1, 0 or 1 according to a number's sign.
use_cases: Classify profit, zero or loss.
notes: The result describes the sign, not the magnitude.

summary: Round down toward negative infinity.
use_cases: Count completed units or periods.
notes: INT differs from FIX for negative non-integers.

summary: Discard the fractional part, rounding toward zero.
use_cases: Truncate a quotient.
notes: FIX(-1.2) is -1, whereas INT(-1.2) is -2.

summary: Return the nonnegative square root.
use_cases: Limit trial division in a prime test.
notes: A negative argument raises Illegal function call. Use ^2 to square a value.

summary: Calculate the sine of an angle in radians.
use_cases: Model periodic motion.
notes: For degrees, multiply by pi/180 before calling. Floating-point approximation applies.

summary: Calculate the cosine of an angle in radians.
use_cases: Calculate a circular horizontal coordinate.
notes: Use radians; trigonometric values are approximate.

summary: Calculate the tangent of an angle in radians.
use_cases: Relate an angle to a slope.
notes: Near odd multiples of pi/2 the result is numerically unstable; avoid those angles.

summary: Return the inverse tangent as an angle in radians.
use_cases: Recover an angle from a slope.
notes: This is a one-argument arctangent, not a two-coordinate atan2.

summary: Calculate the natural logarithm (base e).
use_cases: Explore exponential growth inverses.
notes: Zero and negative arguments raise Illegal function call. For another base use LOG(x)/LOG(base).

summary: Calculate e raised to a numeric power.
use_cases: Explore continuous exponential growth.
notes: Large arguments may raise Overflow. This is not 10 raised to a power.

summary: Convert to a signed 16-bit integer using nearest-even rounding.
parameters: number: numeric expression whose rounded result fits -32768 to 32767.
use_cases: Round an input to an integer deliberately.
notes: Ties round to even; 2.5 becomes 2 and 3.5 becomes 4. Out-of-range results raise Overflow.

summary: Convert a numeric expression to IEEE single precision.
parameters: number: numeric value representable in single precision.
use_cases: Observe single-precision rounding.
notes: Equivalent precision to ! and unsuffixed variable assignment; not legacy MBF.

summary: Convert a numeric expression to IEEE double precision.
use_cases: Store calculations in a # variable.
notes: Conversion cannot recover digits already lost in a single-precision value.

summary: Count the characters in a string.
parameters: text$: string expression, including an empty string.
use_cases: Check a name length.
notes: Counts Unicode characters, not encoded DOS bytes. Numeric arguments raise Type mismatch.

summary: Return the Unicode codepoint of the first character in a string.
parameters: text$: nonempty string; later characters are ignored.
use_cases: Inspect the first character.
notes: An empty string raises Illegal function call; behavior beyond ASCII differs from codepage-based GW-BASIC.

summary: Create a one-character string from a code in 0 through 255.
parameters: code: numeric argument rounded to an integer from 0 to 255.
use_cases: Create punctuation or a double quote.
notes: Maps to Unicode codepoints, not CP437 glyphs; not a general Unicode constructor.

summary: Convert a number to text with a leading space for a nonnegative value.
use_cases: Concatenate a number into a label.
notes: No trailing numeric padding space in the returned string. MID$(STR$(n),2) removes a positive leading space.

summary: Read a decimal numeric prefix from a string.
parameters: text$: string with optional leading whitespace/sign and decimal exponent.
use_cases: Extract a number from a numeric text prefix.
notes: Returns 0 when no decimal prefix is present. Hex/octal strings and legacy embedded-space parsing are not implemented.

summary: Return up to count characters from the beginning of a string.
parameters: count: rounded integer >=0; a count larger than the string returns the entire string.
use_cases: Extract a short prefix.
notes: Count 0 returns an empty string. Negative counts raise Illegal function call.

summary: Return up to count characters from the end of a string.
use_cases: Extract a file suffix.
notes: Count 0 returns an empty string; excessive count returns the whole string.

summary: Extract characters from a one-based start position.
parameters: start: rounded integer >=1; positions start at 1, not 0.
length: optional rounded integer >=0; omit it to read to the end.
use_cases: Extract part of a name.
Remove STR$ numeric padding for pattern output.
notes: A start beyond the end returns an empty string. MID$ assignment is not implemented.

summary: Return a string containing count spaces.
use_cases: Indent a text pattern.
notes: The maximum string size is 32767 characters. Negative counts raise Illegal function call.

summary: Repeat one character count times.
parameters: char$: nonempty string; only its first character is repeated.
code: numeric character code from 0 to 255 instead of char$.
use_cases: Draw a separator.
Repeat a symbol in a text pattern.
notes: An empty character string is illegal. Numeric character codes use CHR$ semantics.

summary: Define a named subroutine with parameters and local variables.
parameters: parameters: optional formal variables supplied by a call.
use_cases: Group reusable drawing or input logic.

END
SUB Greet

END SUB

notes: Not implemented in Ghost BASIC. The example explains legacy syntax and cannot run here.
This is a reference topic, not a promise of complete GW-BASIC/QBasic compatibility.
